name: coupled-particle-catalysis
title: Coupled cell: a Smoldyn particle population catalyses an ODE (particle count sets the ODE rate)

behavior_tests.name: catalysed-product-accumulates
behavior_tests.description: The catalysed ODE product P (emitted as probe_a) accumulates to a positive final value as the particle population drives the rate.

behavior_tests.name: particle-driver-builds
behavior_tests.description: The driving particle C population (emitted as probe_b) grows over the run — the signal that sets the ODE rate is non-trivial.

limitations: The rate coupling is an empirical calibration (effective volume ~0.65×polygon area); faithful near the calibrated regime, drifts outside it.
The concave-up acceleration vs a fixed-rate control is shown in the viz but the acceleration magnitude is not pinned to an acceptance band.
claim: A Smoldyn particle simulator and an SBML-ODE can be coupled inside one cell so that the particle population drives the ODE's kinetics (mode B): the live count of a particle species sets the ODE's rate constant each step, so the ODE product accumulates faster as the particle population builds — a cross-formalism catalysis no single engine expresses.
experiment: Run coupled_particle_catalysis (a small vertex tissue of CoupledCells) for 30 steps. Record one cell's particle C count and ODE product P each step.
outcomes: The time series (viz/coupled-particle-catalysis.html) shows P accumulating with a rate that tracks the particle C count: as the confined A+B→C population builds, the ODE's rate constant rises and P accelerates (concave-up), versus a fixed-rate control that stays linear. Computed live from real Smoldyn (via the 3.11 bridge) + tellurium.

axis.label: The catalysed ODE product P (emitted as probe_a) accumulates to a positive final value as the particle population drives the rate.
The driving particle C population (emitted as probe_b) grows over the run — the signal that sets the ODE rate is non-trivial.

question: Can a Smoldyn particle population drive an ODE's kinetics inside one cell, so the ODE product accelerates as the particle count builds (mode B)?

study_card.goal: Show that a particle population drives an ODE's kinetics (mode B) inside one cell.
study_card.mechanism: A Smoldyn particle population (A+B->C, confined to the cell polygon) catalyses an ODE S->P: the live particle C count sets the ODE rate constant each step, so the product accumulates faster as the population grows.
study_card.why_before_next: Mode B couples stochastic spatial chemistry to a continuous ODE — the cross-formalism direction the other motifs reuse to let particle counts modulate metabolism.
study_card.expected_result: The ODE product accumulates (P>0) while the particle driver grows, so the particle population genuinely sets the ODE kinetics.
study_card.main_expert_question: The rate map is an empirical effective-volume calibration (~0.65x polygon area); over what conversion regime does it stay faithful before it needs re-fitting?
